tools.name: cancel_event
tools.description: Cancel an event, or one occurrence of a repeating one. A whole event is deleted; one occurrence is marked canceled, which is how a single date leaves a series — the result says which of the two happened. Google keeps the record either way, and list_events with show_canceled still shows it. `scope` is REQUIRED when the event repeats, and there is no default because the same words mean three different things: `instance` changes one occurrence, `series` changes all of them, and `this_and_following` changes this occurrence and every later one. Name the occurrence with the occurrence's own id, or with the series id plus `original_start` — the scheduled start, which list_instances reports, and which still identifies an occurrence somebody has moved. With `this_and_following` the series simply ends before this occurrence, which is one call rather than the two an update takes. `notify` is REQUIRED whenever the write can reach another person, and this server has no default in either direction: `none` asks Google to email nobody, `external_only` emails the guests outside your own organization, `all` emails every guest. `none` is refused outright when a guest is outside your organization, because such a guest may have no Google Calendar for the event to appear in and email is then the only way they can learn of it. Whatever you pass, the result says what was ASKED FOR — Google reports nothing about what arrived, and `none` is not a promise of silence. Read that rule twice here: canceling with no notification removes the meeting from YOUR calendar and leaves it on your guests'. They will still turn up. Every write is a patch under If-Match, so it is refused as `[stale]` rather than overwriting somebody who changed this first. Pass `etag` from the get_event you decided on to be held to that exact version; pass `force: true` only when you genuinely mean "whatever it says now". `dry_run: true` reports exactly what would change and how many guests would be emailed, without writing anything. Use it when you are not certain which event or which occurrence you have.

calendar.description: The calendar the event is on.

dry_run.description: Report what would be canceled and who would be emailed, without writing.

etag.description: The etag from the get_event you decided on.

event_id.description: The event id, or the series id when original_start names the occurrence.

force.description: Cancel with If-Match: * rather than being refused if somebody changed it first.

notify.description: Who Google is asked to email: none, external_only or all. Required when the event has guests — with none, the guests keep the meeting.

original_start.description: The occurrence's SCHEDULED start, from list_instances.

scope.description: Required when the event repeats: instance, series or this_and_following.

time_zone.description: IANA zone to read original_start and show the times in.

tools.name: check_availability
tools.description: When people are busy, and when they are free, in a window. `from` and `to` are required and take either a yyyy-mm-dd date or an RFC3339 timestamp. A bare date means that whole day in the resolved zone, so from and to on the same date is that one day. Resolve relative expressions like "next Tuesday" yourself before calling: this server does not guess, and the result always echoes the absolute window and the zone it used so you can check the resolution. Times are shown in `time_zone` if you pass one, otherwise the calendar's own zone, otherwise the zone in the account's Calendar settings. The result names which of the three it used. This server never falls back to the machine's own clock zone. This asks Google's free/busy service rather than listing events, which matters: it sees busy time on calendars whose events you cannot read, and it respects events marked "free", so a list of events is not the same answer. A calendar that could not be read comes back as UNKNOWN, never as free — do not book over it. The result also reports the gaps when nobody is busy; min_minutes drops the ones too short to use. Working hours are not applied: pass a narrower window if you only want office hours. Calendars are asked in batches of 50, and the result says how many requests that took.

calendars.description: Calendar ids, email addresses or titles. Defaults to the account's primary calendar. An address works even for a calendar you cannot read.

from.description: Start of the window: yyyy-mm-dd or RFC3339. Required.

min_minutes.description: Ignore free gaps shorter than this many minutes.

time_zone.description: IANA zone to read the window and show the times in.

to.description: End of the window: yyyy-mm-dd or RFC3339. Required.

tools.name: create_event
tools.description: Create an event. `start` and `end` are either two yyyy-mm-dd dates for an all-day event, where `end` is the LAST day and is included, or two RFC3339 timestamps for a timed one — never one of each, because a date is not a time. Times are written in `time_zone` if you pass one, otherwise the calendar's own zone; the result says which it used, and the zone is always sent alongside the timestamp so a repeating event keeps its wall-clock time across a daylight-saving change. `recurrence` takes RFC 5545 lines such as RRULE:FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=TU;COUNT=10. `notify` is REQUIRED whenever the write can reach another person, and this server has no default in either direction: `none` asks Google to email nobody, `external_only` emails the guests outside your own organization, `all` emails every guest. `none` is refused outright when a guest is outside your organization, because such a guest may have no Google Calendar for the event to appear in and email is then the only way they can learn of it. Whatever you pass, the result says what was ASKED FOR — Google reports nothing about what arrived, and `none` is not a promise of silence. `dry_run: true` reports exactly what would change and how many guests would be emailed, without writing anything. Use it when you are not certain which event or which occurrence you have.

calendar.description: The calendar id or title to create it on. Defaults to the account's primary calendar.

dry_run.description: Report what would be created and who would be emailed, without writing.

end.description: End: for an all-day event the LAST day, included; for a timed one an RFC3339 timestamp. Must be the same kind as start. Required.

free_not_busy.description: Mark the time as free rather than busy, so it does not block availability.

guests.description: Email addresses to invite. Passing any of these makes notify required.

notify.description: Who Google is asked to email: none, external_only or all. Required when the event has guests.

start.description: Start: yyyy-mm-dd for an all-day event, or RFC3339 for a timed one. Required.

time_zone.description: IANA zone the times are written in, such as Europe/Copenhagen. Defaults to the calendar's own.

title.description: What the event is called. Required.

tools.name: get_calendar
tools.description: One calendar in full: its description, time zone, your access level, and who else it is shared with. Use list_calendars to see every calendar; use this when you need the sharing list or are checking whether you may write somewhere.

calendar.description: The calendar id, its title, or "primary" for the account's own calendar.

tools.name: get_event
tools.description: One event in full, including its guests and their responses, its recurrence rule if it has one, and its etag. Times are shown in `time_zone` if you pass one, otherwise the calendar's own zone, otherwise the zone in the account's Calendar settings. The result names which of the three it used. This server never falls back to the machine's own clock zone. An event id is unique per calendar and not globally, so `calendar` is required alongside it. Ids come from list_events or search_events.

calendar.description: The calendar the event is on. An event id is unique per calendar, not globally.

event_id.description: The event id, from list_events or search_events.

time_zone.description: IANA zone to show the times in.

tools.name: get_settings
tools.description: The account's own Calendar settings: its time zone, which day the week starts on, and the color palette. The time zone here is the last fallback for every other tool, so read it when you need to know what "today" or "9am" means for this person.

tools.name: list_calendars
tools.description: List the calendars this account can see, with each one's id, time zone and your access level. Start here: every other tool takes a calendar, the ids come from this list, and the time zone it reports is what dates and times elsewhere are read against. It is cheap. Use get_calendar for one calendar's description and who it is shared with.

include_hidden.description: Include calendars hidden in the Calendar UI.

tools.name: list_events
tools.description: Read a schedule: the events on one or more calendars in a window. `from` and `to` are required and take either a yyyy-mm-dd date or an RFC3339 timestamp. A bare date means that whole day in the resolved zone, so from and to on the same date is that one day. Resolve relative expressions like "next Tuesday" yourself before calling: this server does not guess, and the result always echoes the absolute window and the zone it used so you can check the resolution. Times are shown in `time_zone` if you pass one, otherwise the calendar's own zone, otherwise the zone in the account's Calendar settings. The result names which of the three it used. This server never falls back to the machine's own clock zone. `expand` decides which shape you get, and the two are genuinely different: with expand=true (the default) a repeating event appears as each of its occurrences, which is what you want to answer "what is on this week". With expand=false it appears once, as a series with its recurrence rule, which is what you want before changing the whole series. Canceled events are hidden unless show_canceled is set. Use search_events to find an event by text; use check_availability to find free time, because a list of events is not the same as being free.

calendars.description: Calendar ids or titles. Defaults to the account's primary calendar.

from.description: Start of the window: yyyy-mm-dd or RFC3339. Required.

max_events.description: Cap on events returned. The server has its own budget and says when it truncated.

no_expand.description: Return repeating events once as a series with its rule, instead of as each occurrence.

page_token.description: Continue a truncated read, from next_page_token.

show_canceled.description: Include canceled events, which are hidden by default.

time_zone.description: IANA zone to read the window and show the times in, such as Europe/Copenhagen.

to.description: End of the window: yyyy-mm-dd or RFC3339. Required. A bare date means the end of that day.

tools.name: list_instances
tools.description: The occurrences of one repeating event. `event_id` is the SERIES id, which list_events reports as series_id on each occurrence — an occurrence's own id is not a series id. Pass both from and to for a window, or neither for the whole series. Times are shown in `time_zone` if you pass one, otherwise the calendar's own zone, otherwise the zone in the account's Calendar settings. The result names which of the three it used. This server never falls back to the machine's own clock zone. Each occurrence reports its own id, and says when it was moved from its scheduled time. Canceled occurrences are hidden unless show_canceled is set, and a canceled occurrence is how one date is removed from a series — so pass it when you need to know which dates are gone. Use get_event on the series id to see the recurrence rule itself.

calendar.description: The calendar the series is on.

event_id.description: The repeating event's id. On an occurrence from list_events this is its series_id, not its own id.

from.description: Start of the window: yyyy-mm-dd or RFC3339. Pass both from and to, or neither.

max_events.description: Cap on occurrences returned. The server has its own budget and says when it truncated.

page_token.description: Continue a truncated read, from next_page_token.

show_canceled.description: Include occurrences that were canceled, which is how single dates are removed from a series.

time_zone.description: IANA zone to show the occurrences in.

to.description: End of the window: yyyy-mm-dd or RFC3339. Pass both from and to, or neither.

tools.name: move_event
tools.description: Move an event to another calendar, which changes who organizes it. The event keeps its id but is addressed on the new calendar from then on. This does NOT change the time — use update_event for that. `scope` is REQUIRED when the event repeats, and there is no default because the same words mean three different things: `instance` changes one occurrence, `series` changes all of them, and `this_and_following` changes this occurrence and every later one. Name the occurrence with the occurrence's own id, or with the series id plus `original_start` — the scheduled start, which list_instances reports, and which still identifies an occurrence somebody has moved. `this_and_following` is not available here: there is nothing to split when the event is simply changing calendars. `notify` is REQUIRED whenever the write can reach another person, and this server has no default in either direction: `none` asks Google to email nobody, `external_only` emails the guests outside your own organization, `all` emails every guest. `none` is refused outright when a guest is outside your organization, because such a guest may have no Google Calendar for the event to appear in and email is then the only way they can learn of it. Whatever you pass, the result says what was ASKED FOR — Google reports nothing about what arrived, and `none` is not a promise of silence. This is the ONE write that is not made under If-Match — events.move is not a patch — so it takes no etag and is not refused if somebody changed the event since you read it. `dry_run: true` reports exactly what would change and how many guests would be emailed, without writing anything. Use it when you are not certain which event or which occurrence you have.

calendar.description: The calendar the event is on now.

dry_run.description: Report what would move and who would be emailed, without writing.

notify.description: Who Google is asked to email: none, external_only or all. Required when the event has guests.

original_start.description: The occurrence's SCHEDULED start, when moving one occurrence of a series.

scope.description: Required when the event repeats: instance or series.

time_zone.description: IANA zone to show the times in.

to_calendar.description: The calendar id or title to move it to. Required.

tools.name: respond_to_event
tools.description: Answer an invitation: accepted, declined or tentative, with an optional comment. This changes only THIS account's response and nothing else on the event — which is why it is a separate tool rather than an update. Do not RSVP by patching the guest list; that overwrites everybody else's answer. `scope` is REQUIRED when the event repeats, and there is no default because the same words mean three different things: `instance` changes one occurrence, `series` changes all of them, and `this_and_following` changes this occurrence and every later one. Name the occurrence with the occurrence's own id, or with the series id plus `original_start` — the scheduled start, which list_instances reports, and which still identifies an occurrence somebody has moved. `this_and_following` is not available here: answering some occurrences and not others would mean rewriting somebody else's series. `notify` is REQUIRED whenever the write can reach another person, and this server has no default in either direction: `none` asks Google to email nobody, `external_only` emails the guests outside your own organization, `all` emails every guest. `none` is refused outright when a guest is outside your organization, because such a guest may have no Google Calendar for the event to appear in and email is then the only way they can learn of it. Whatever you pass, the result says what was ASKED FOR — Google reports nothing about what arrived, and `none` is not a promise of silence. `dry_run: true` reports exactly what would change and how many guests would be emailed, without writing anything. Use it when you are not certain which event or which occurrence you have.

calendar.description: The calendar the invitation is on.

comment.description: A note that goes alongside the answer.

dry_run.description: Report what would change and who would be emailed, without writing.

etag.description: The etag from the get_event you decided on.

event_id.description: The event id, or the series id when original_start names the occurrence.

force.description: Answer with If-Match: * rather than being refused if somebody changed it first.

notify.description: Who Google is asked to email: none, external_only or all. Required when the event has guests.

original_start.description: The occurrence's SCHEDULED start, when answering for one occurrence.

scope.description: Required when the event repeats: instance or series.

time_zone.description: IANA zone to show the times in.

tools.name: search_events
tools.description: Find events matching free text in a window. `from` and `to` are required and take either a yyyy-mm-dd date or an RFC3339 timestamp. A bare date means that whole day in the resolved zone, so from and to on the same date is that one day. Resolve relative expressions like "next Tuesday" yourself before calling: this server does not guess, and the result always echoes the absolute window and the zone it used so you can check the resolution. Important: Google's event search is undocumented free text with no field scoping — you cannot search "attendee:someone" or restrict it to titles, and Google does not say which fields it reads. Treat an empty result as "this search found nothing", not as "there is no such event", and fall back to list_events over the window when you need certainty. Searching several calendars costs one request each.

calendars.description: Calendar ids or titles. Defaults to the primary calendar.

from.description: Start of the window: yyyy-mm-dd or RFC3339. Required.

page_token.description: Continue a truncated search, from next_page_token.

query.description: Free text. Google decides which fields this matches; there is no field syntax.

time_zone.description: IANA zone to read the window and show the times in.

to.description: End of the window: yyyy-mm-dd or RFC3339. Required.

tools.name: update_event
tools.description: Change an event. Only the fields you pass are touched; everything else is left exactly as it is, so this can never drop a guest list or flatten a series the way a whole-resource write does. Guests are added and removed one at a time with `add_guests` and `remove_guests`, applied to the list as it is read, so somebody else's RSVP arriving in between is reported rather than overwritten. `scope` is REQUIRED when the event repeats, and there is no default because the same words mean three different things: `instance` changes one occurrence, `series` changes all of them, and `this_and_following` changes this occurrence and every later one. Name the occurrence with the occurrence's own id, or with the series id plus `original_start` — the scheduled start, which list_instances reports, and which still identifies an occurrence somebody has moved. `this_and_following` is two calls: the original series is ended before this occurrence and a NEW series starts at it with a new id, and any exception after this occurrence is reset. The result says so. `notify` is REQUIRED whenever the write can reach another person, and this server has no default in either direction: `none` asks Google to email nobody, `external_only` emails the guests outside your own organization, `all` emails every guest. `none` is refused outright when a guest is outside your organization, because such a guest may have no Google Calendar for the event to appear in and email is then the only way they can learn of it. Whatever you pass, the result says what was ASKED FOR — Google reports nothing about what arrived, and `none` is not a promise of silence. Every write is a patch under If-Match, so it is refused as `[stale]` rather than overwriting somebody who changed this first. Pass `etag` from the get_event you decided on to be held to that exact version; pass `force: true` only when you genuinely mean "whatever it says now". `dry_run: true` reports exactly what would change and how many guests would be emailed, without writing anything. Use it when you are not certain which event or which occurrence you have. Use respond_to_event to answer an invitation and move_event to change which calendar it is on.

add_guests.description: Email addresses to invite, added to the guests already there.

calendar.description: The calendar the event is on. An event id is unique per calendar, not globally.

description.description: New description. Omit to leave it; pass an empty string to clear it.

dry_run.description: Report what would change and who would be emailed, without writing.

end.description: New end. For an all-day event this is the last day, included.

etag.description: The etag from the get_event you decided on. The write is refused as stale if it moved since.

event_id.description: The event id, or the series id when original_start names the occurrence.

force.description: Write with If-Match: * — overwrite whatever it says now, rather than being refused if somebody changed it.

free_not_busy.description: Mark the time free rather than busy.

location.description: New location. Omit to leave it; pass an empty string to clear it.

notify.description: Who Google is asked to email: none, external_only or all. Required when the event has guests.

original_start.description: The occurrence's SCHEDULED start, from list_instances. Use it with the series id to name one occurrence.

recurrence.description: New RFC 5545 lines. An empty list stops the event repeating.

scope.description: Required when the event repeats: instance, series or this_and_following.

start.description: New start: yyyy-mm-dd or RFC3339, matching what the event already is.

time_zone.description: IANA zone the new times are written in.

title.description: New title. Omit to leave it; pass an empty string to clear it.
